record.paper_title: Open Questions about Ramsey-Type Statements in Reverse Mathematics
record.context_brief: Low_n solutions for FS^n and TS^n
record.original_question: For each n at least 3, does every computable instance of the free set theorem FS^n, and likewise every computable instance of the thin set theorem TS^n, admit a low_n solution?

evidence.quote: Question 5.3 For every n ≥ 3, does every computable instance of FSn (resp. TSn ) admit a lown solution?
By Cholak et al. [8], every computable instance of FS2 and TS2 admit a low2 solution. Therefore FS2 (hence TS2 ) are strictly weaker than TS3 (hence FS3 ) over RCA0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of computability theory on the natural numbers ω. For a finite set X ⊂ ω write [X]^n for the family of n-element subsets of X (identified with strictly increasing n-tuples), and similarly for [ω]^n.

Definitions.
- Free set theorem FS^n. Given a function f : [ω]^n → ω, an infinite set H ⊆ ω is f-free if for every σ ∈ [H]^n, whenever f(σ) ∈ H then f(σ) ∈ σ. The principle FS^n asserts that every f : [ω]^n → ω admits an infinite f-free set. An instance of FS^n is such a function f, and a solution is an infinite f-free set.
- Thin set theorem TS^n. Given f : [ω]^n → ω, an infinite set H ⊆ ω is f-thin if f([H]^n) ≠ ω, i.e. f restricted to [H]^n omits at least one value. The principle TS^n asserts that every f : [ω]^n → ω has an infinite f-thin set. Instances and solutions are defined accordingly.
- Lowness. For k ≥ 1, a set A ⊆ ω is low_k if (A)^{(k)} ≡_T ∅^{(k)}, where X^{(k)} denotes the k-th Turing jump of X. An instance f is computable if it is computable as a function ω → ω (with [ω]^n coded canonically).

Question. Fix an integer n ≥ 3. Does every computable instance of FS^n admit a low_n solution? Likewise, does every computable instance of TS^n admit a low_n solution?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for surveys and recent work on the free set and thin set theorems (Cholak–Patey on cone avoidance for thin sets, Liu–Patey on the reverse mathematics of thin set and Erdős–Moser, and related papers) reveal substantial activity around computational strength, cone avoidance, and combinatorial weakness of FS^n and TS^n for n ≥ 3, but no source found announces a low_n solution result for arbitrary computable instances of FS^n or TS^n when n ≥ 3. The lown-result for n = 2 (Cholak–Jockusch–Slaman style) is the only confirmed case; for n ≥ 3 the question still appears open.

status_evidence.title: Thin set theorems and cone avoidance (Cholak–Patey)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes cone avoidance and strong cone avoidance thresholds for thin set theorems but does not establish low_n solutions for FS^n / TS^n at n≥3.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on TS^n focuses on cone avoidance rather than lowness; no low_n result for n≥3 is announced.

status_evidence.title: The reverse mathematics of the Thin set and Erdős–Moser theorems (Liu–Patey)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies combinatorial weakness of TS^n and FS^n; addresses non-implications with EM but does not resolve low_n solutions for n≥3.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent reverse-mathematical work on FS^n / TS^n does not resolve the low_n question for n≥3.

status_evidence.title: Open Questions in Reverse Mathematics (Montalbán)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions about lowness and Ramsey-type principles in reverse mathematics.
status_evidence.claim: Lowness questions for higher-arity Ramsey-type principles remain a recognized open area.
